column1: # Mutant batch for the history-picker change — history moves from a chip
# ListView in the bubble's overlay window to an icon button plus a searchable
# floating picker Activity.
#   scripts/mutate.sh batch scripts/mutants/history-picker.tsv
# Tab-separated: NAME <TAB> FILE <TAB> FROM <TAB> TO [<TAB> TEST_FILTER]
# FROM must occur EXACTLY ONCE in FILE or the mutant is refused. Every FROM
# below was checked for single occurrence before the row was written.
# 🔴 DEFINITIONS ONLY, NEVER RESULTS. A verdict is void the moment the tree
# moves — see scripts/MUTATION-TESTING.md. The verdicts these produced live in
# the pull request for this change, stamped with the commit they were measured
# on.
# 🔴 WHY THIS BATCH EXISTS AT ALL. Exactly ONE test in this change is
# regression coverage —
# HistoryPickerActivityTest.tappingARowOpensTheCardOnThatDictationThroughDictateLaunch,
# re-homed from the deleted BubbleHistoryRevealTest, which pinned behaviour the
# operator kept. Everything else is an INVARIANT GUARD: the activity, the
# shell, the launcher, the row and the button all arrive with the change, so
# "red at the base commit" would be a compile error rather than a guard watched
# failing. This batch is what stands in for red-at-base.
# 🔴 EACH ROW BREAKS ONE EXPRESSION AND NAMES THE CLASS WHOSE OWN ASSERTION
# MUST GO RED, so a kill is attributable to that expression and is credited to
# a guard that actually executed. Where one mutation is the subject of two
# different classes' claims it is listed TWICE with two filters (m-hist02 /
# m-hist03, m-hist12 / m-hist13, m-hist16 / m-hist17) rather than filtered
# loosely — a kill by "something noticed" is not a statement about either
# guard.
# 🔴 ISOLATION. Every mutant leaves the branch structure intact. m-hist05 and
# m-hist18/19 replace a sub-expression INSIDE a conditional rather than
# deleting the conditional, which is what scripts/MUTATION-TESTING.md requires:
# a mutant that removes a guard together with its enclosing condition proves
# nothing about the guard and dies for the wrong reason. m-hist12/13 insert a
# `return` AFTER the subclass hook so only the shell's finish() is removed —
# the hook still runs, so the clipboard write and the card launch are
# unaffected and the kill is attributable to finish() alone.
# 🔴 WHAT THIS BATCH CANNOT VALIDATE, stated so a clean sweep is not
# over-read:
#  * PickerShellSeamLedgerTest's growth/shrink arms. Taking a picker off the
#    shell is not a narrow expression — it is a compile error, because the
#    shell's abstract members become unimplemented. Those arms carry their own
#    in-test controls instead (theSuperclassScanSeesAThirdPickerHoweverItIs...,
#    theLedgerWouldGoRedOnBothAThirdPickerAndADepartedOne), which mutate the
#    scan's INPUT rather than the tree.
#  * Anything about appearance, layout or IME focus. Robolectric lays nothing
#    out and has no input method; the two-button reveal's look and the picker's
#    real search-field focus are device claims.
